title: Minimum Stability Factor of Array
summary: Given an integer array and a maximum number of modifications, find the minimum stability factor of the array after making at most the specified modifications.
statement: Given an integer array and a maximum number of modifications, find the minimum stability factor of the array after making at most the specified modifications. A subarray is stable if its highest common factor is at least 2. The stability factor is the length of the longest stable subarray. If no stable subarray remains, return 0. The highest common factor of an array is the largest integer that divides all elements without a remainder. A subarray of length 1 is stable if its single element is at least 2.
constraints: A stable subarray has GCD at least two.
Change at most maxC values arbitrarily to minimize the longest stable length.
hints: Bounding stability by L means every stable window of length L+1 must be hit by a change.
Use a GCD sparse table and greedily change the right endpoint of each unhit violating window.
Count right-endpoint changes, then binary search the smallest feasible L.
Equal-length violating windows are intervals; earliest-ending greedy stabbing minimizes changes, and GCD queries verify each interval.
editorial: Equal-length violating windows are intervals; earliest-ending greedy stabbing minimizes changes, and GCD queries verify each interval.

tests.explanation: Changing five breaks the only stable length-two subarray, leaving stability one.
Two changes can destroy every stable subarray longer than one.
